# **The Ranger**

***Far from the bustle of cities and towns, past the hedges that shelter the most distant farms from the terrors of the wild, amid the dense-packed trees of trackless forests and across wide and empty plains, rangers keep their unending watch.***  
*You must have a Dexterity and a Wisdom modifier of \+1 or higher in order to multiclass in or out of this class.*

## **Class Features**

### **Vitals**

**Hit Dice:** 1d10  
**Hit Points at 1st Level**: 10 \+ your Constitution modifier  
**Hit Points at Higher Levels:** 1d10 (or 6\) \+ your Constitution modifier per ranger level after 1st  
**Stress Points at 1st Level:** 3 \+ your Constitution modifier

### **Proficiencies**

**Armor:** Light armor, medium armor, shields  
**Weapons:** Simple weapons, martial weapons  
**Tools:** None  
**Skills:** Choose three from Animal Handling, Athletics, Insight, Investigation, Nature, Perception, Stealth, and Survival

### **Equipment**

You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:

* (a) scale mail or (b) leather armor  
* (a) two shortswords or (b) two simple melee weapons  
* (a) a dungeoneer's pack or (b) an explorer's pack  
* A longbow and a quiver of 20 arrows

### **Hunter’s Mark**

Also at 1st level, you can channel natural magics to mark your quarry. As a Minor Action, take a Stress and choose a creature you can see within 90 ft. For 1 hour, you deal an additional d6 of damage to the target when you hit it with a weapon attack. Also, you have advantage on any Wisdom (Perception) or Wisdom (Survival) check you make to find it. If the target drops to 0 hit points before this effect ends, you can immediately unflip a Martial Prowess.

At 9th and 15th level, the damage die of Hunter’s Mark becomes a d8 and a d10, respectively.

### **Martial Prowess**

Your experience as a hunter or nomad has taught you special techniques to utilize against your foes. You know one Prowess from the Ranger prowess list.

**Prowesses Known.** The Ranger table shows how many Prowesses you know at 1st level and higher. When you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the Martial Prowesses you know and replace it with another Prowess from the Ranger prowess list.

**Prowess Ability.** Wisdom, whichever is higher, is your Prowess ability for your Ranger prowesses, as the power of your abilities relies on your physical capacity. You use your Wisdom whenever a prowess refers to your prowess ability. In addition, you use your Wisdom modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a ranger Prowess you use.

**Prowess save DC** \= 8 \+ your proficiency bonus \+ your Wisdom modifier

### **Spellcasting**

By the time you reach 2nd level, you have learned to use the magical essence of nature to cast spells, much as a druid does.

**Spell Slots**  
The Ranger table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your ranger spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these spells, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long rest.

For example, if you know the 1st-level spell Animal Friendship and have a 1st-level and a 2nd-level spell slot available, you can cast Animal Friendship using either slot.

**Spells Known of 1st Level and Higher**  
You know two 1st-level spells of your choice from the ranger spell list.

The Spells Known column of the Ranger table shows when you learn more ranger spells of your choice. Each of these spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For instance, when you reach 5th level in this class, you can learn one new spell of 1st or 2nd level.

Additionally, when you gain a level in this class, you can choose one of the ranger spells you know and replace it with another spell from the ranger spell list, which also must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

**Spellcasting Ability**  
Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your ranger spells, since your magic draws on your attunement to nature. You use your Wisdom whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Wisdom modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a ranger spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.

**Spell save DC** \= 8 \+ your proficiency bonus \+ your Wisdom modifier

**Spell attack modifier** \= your proficiency bonus \+ your Wisdom modifier

### **Trait Improvement**

When you reach 2nd level, and again at 4th, 6th, 8th, 10th, 12th, 14th, 16th, and 19th level, you can improve upon one of your traits listed below. You have the following choices:

* Gain an additional Stress Slot  
* Gain a \+1 bonus to a Saving Throw  
* Gain a \+1 bonus to your Initiative  
* Gain proficiency in a skill, tool, or language. This option may only be chosen twice.

### **Favored Enemy**

At 3rd level, you have significant experience studying, tracking, and hunting a certain type of enemy.

Choose a type of favored enemy: Mundane (humanoids, plants, beasts), Monsters (aberrations, monstrosities, undead), Primordials (dragons, giants, elementals, oozes), and Immortals (celestials, fey, fiends).

When you apply your Hunter’s Mark to your Favored Enemy, its dice category is increased (to a maximum of d12). Also, you have advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks to track your favored enemies, Intelligence checks to recall information about them.

### **Ranger Conclave**

At 3rd level, you choose to emulate the ideals and training of a ranger conclave. Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 7th, 11th, and 15th level.

| Martial Archetype |  |  |  |  |
| :---- | ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- |
| Beastmaster |  |  |  |  |

### **Ability Improvement**

When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 14th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase two ability modifiers of your choice by 1\. Alternatively, you can increase only one ability modifier of your choice by 1 and gain a Feat. As normal, you can't increase an ability modifier above \+5 using this feature.

### **Extra Attack**

Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

### **Signature Prowess**

Beginning at 5th level, you can choose a Martial Prowess to make your signature. When you use that Prowess for the first time, rotate the card instead of flipping it. When you use a rotated Prowess, you then flip it.

The number of Signature Prowesses you have increases to two at 9th level and to three at 17th level.

### **Feral Senses**

At 18th level, you gain preternatural senses that help you fight creatures you can't see. When you attack a creature you can't see, your inability to see it doesn't impose disadvantage on your attack rolls against it.

You are also aware of the location of any invisible creature within 30 feet of you, provided that the creature isn't hidden from you and you aren't blinded or deafened.

### **Thrill of the Hunt**

At 20th level, you become so engrossed in the chasing of your prey that you feel a surge of energy whenever one is finished. When the target of your Hunter’s Mark is reduced to 0 Hit Points: your movement, Minor Action, and Major Action are restored. This can only happen once per long rest.

# **Beastmaster**

***The Beast Master archetype embodies a friendship between the civilized races and the beasts of the world. United in focus, beast and ranger work as one to fight the monstrous foes that threaten civilization and the wilderness alike. Emulating the Beast Master archetype means committing yourself to this ideal, working in partnership with an animal as its companion and friend.***

| Beastmaster |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Level** | **Features** |
| 3rd | Ranger’s Companion, Beastmaster Prowesses |
| 7th | Exceptional Training |
| 11th | Bestial Fury |
| 15th | Share Spells |

## **Ranger’s Companion**

At 3rd level, you gain a companion that accompanies you on your adventures and has magically bonded with you. Choose a beast, monstrosity, aberration, or dragon that is no larger than Medium, and that has a challenge rating of ¼ or lower. You should work with your DM to determine if the creature you choose is allowed and how you managed to acquire it as your companion. While you are bonded with the companion, they gain the following benefits:

* It adds your proficiency bonus to its AC, attack rolls, damage rolls, skills it is proficient in, and all saving throws.  
* Its hit point maximum equals its normal maximum or four times your ranger level, whichever is higher.  
* During a short rest, it can take the Tend action to heal itself, or the Relax move to restore your Stress.

The companion obeys your commands as best as it can. It takes its turn on your initiative. It can move and use its Reactions on its own, but it will only take actions when you command it to as a Minor Action. Once per turn, you may take Stress to command your Companion without using a Minor Action. Your companion may use your Martial Prowesses, provided the Prowess describes an action the companion is physically capable of performing.

If you are incapacitated or absent, the companion acts on its own, focusing on protecting you and itself. 

When the companion is reduced to 0 Hit Points, you should work with your DM to determine if it begins making death saving throws, is shielded from permanent death by magic, or is otherwise dispelled. Regardless of the method, if the companion is or would be killed, you may restore or replace it at the end of your next long rest.

## **Beastmaster Prowess**

Also at 3rd level, you learn an additional spell when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown in the Beastmaster Prowesses table. Each Prowess counts as a ranger Prowess for you, but it doesn't count against the number of ranger Prowess you know.

| Beastmaster Prowesses |  |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Level** | **Features** |
| 3rd | Find by Scent |
| 5th | Grappling Strike |
| 9th | Beast’s Intuition |
| 13th | One by One |
| 17th | Unbreakable Bond |

## **Exceptional Training**

Beginning at 7th level, your companion has grown far stronger as a result of your training, granting it the following benefits:

* When you command your beast companion to take the Attack action, the companion can make two attacks, or it can take the Multiattack action if it has that action.   
* The companion’s attacks also count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.  
* The companion’s attacks also benefit from creature’s marked by Hunter’s Mark.

## **Improved Ranger’s Companion**

Starting at 11th level, your mastery over your bond allows you to command far more powerful creatures. You may now have a companion that is a beast, monstrosity, aberration, or dragon that is no larger than Large and has a challenge rating of 1 or lower. Its hit point maximum equals its normal maximum or five times your ranger level, whichever is higher.

If you choose to keep your existing companion, you may instead grant it a new form that follows these restrictions, representing the companion growing stronger alongside you. One common way to do this is to grant the companion a Dire form, which reflects increased size, strength, and resilience. When a companion gains a Dire form, it gains the following benefits:

* Its size increases to Large, if it was smaller.  
* Its AC increases by 1  
* It gains a \+2 bonus to its Strength modifier.  
* It gains a \+1 bonus to its Constitution modifier.  
* The damage die of its attacks increases by one step to a maximum of d12.

The companion retains its personality, memories, and bond with you, regardless of whether it takes on a new form or is replaced by a different creature.

## **Share Spells**

Beginning at 15th level, when you cast a spell targeting yourself, you can also affect your beast companion with the spell if the beast is within 30 feet of you.
